schemes.officialName: Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT 1.0)
schemes.description: Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT 1.0) is a centrally sponsored scheme launched by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) to provide basic infrastructure services such as water supply, sewerage, septage management, storm water drainage, green spaces, and…
schemes.objective: - Ensure that every household has access to a tap with assured supply of water and a sewerage connection - Increase the amenity value of cities by developing greenery and well-maintained open spaces (e.g., parks) - Reduce pollution by switching to public transport or constructing facilities for non-motorized transport (e.g., walking and cycling) - Strengthen institutional and financial capacity of Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) for effective service delivery - Promote reforms in urban governance and service delivery through incentive-based mechanisms
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), Government of India

benefits.detail: The mission promotes convergence with other schemes like Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban), Housing for All (Urban), and Smart Cities Mission.

benefits.detail: It also encourages public-private partnerships (PPPs) and aims to improve service delivery and urban governance through institutional reforms and capacity building of ULBs.

schemes.description: The Viability Gap Funding (VGF) Scheme is a flagship initiative of the Government of India under the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA) that provides financial assistance to financially unviable but socially/economically desirable Public Private Partnership (PPP) projects.
schemes.objective: - Promote PPPs to bring private efficiencies and attract private capital in infrastructure development - Provide financial assistance to financially unviable but socially/economically desirable PPP projects - Attract more PPP projects and facilitate private investment in social sectors (Health, Education, Wastewater, Solid Waste Management, Water Supply etc.) - Support infrastructure development in sectors with long gestation periods and limited financial returns - Increase the quality and quantity of bankable PPP projects through financial viability enhancement
schemes.ministry: Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, Government of India

benefits.name: support in the form of viability gap funding
benefits.detail: Financial support in the form of viability gap funding grants to cover project costs.

benefits.name: For social sector projects
benefits.detail: For social sector projects: up to 80% of Capex and up to 50% of Opex for 5 years after Commercial Operation Date (CoD).

benefits.detail: Sub Scheme-1 (social sectors): Central Government provides up to 30% of Capex, with State Government/Sponsoring Central Ministry/Statutory Entity providing additional support up to 30% of Capex.

schemes.description: The MSME Pre-Pack Insolvency Resolution Process (PPIRP) is a streamlined insolvency resolution mechanism under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, designed specifically for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to facilitate faster and cost-effective resolution of financial distress.
schemes.objective: - Facilitate faster resolution of insolvency for MSMEs - Reduce the cost and time associated with the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) - Enable the corporate debtor to initiate resolution with creditor consent - Preserve business continuity and maximize value for stakeholders - Provide a mechanism for early identification and exclusion of non-viable projects - Strengthen project-wise ring-fencing of funds and accounts in real estate insolvency (as part of broader IBC framework) - Ensure timely handover of possession to allottees in real estate projects - Enhance transparency and
schemes.ministry: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India

benefits.name: PPIRP offers a faster resolution timeline
benefits.detail: PPIRP offers a faster resolution timeline (typically within 90 days) compared to regular CIRP (180 days, extendable to 330 days).

benefits.name: It reduces procedural costs by avoiding public invitation of
benefits.detail: It reduces procedural costs by avoiding public invitation of resolution plans and e-auctions.

benefits.name: process allows the existing management to retain control
benefits.detail: The process allows the existing management to retain control if the resolution plan is approved, promoting business continuity.

benefits.name: It provides flexibility in structuring the resolution plan, including
benefits.detail: It provides flexibility in structuring the resolution plan, including merger, amalgamation, or takeover.

benefits.name: Creditors benefit from higher realization due to reduced delays
benefits.detail: Creditors benefit from higher realization due to reduced delays and preservation of going concern value.

benefits.name: process also minimizes disruption to ongoing operations and
benefits.detail: The process also minimizes disruption to ongoing operations and preserves employment.

benefits.name: PPIRP does not involve direct financial support from the
benefits.detail: PPIRP does not involve direct financial support from the government.

benefits.name: Instead, it facilitates resolution through private infusion of funds
benefits.detail: Instead, it facilitates resolution through private infusion of funds by the resolution applicant, which may include fresh equity, quasi-equity, or internal accruals.

benefits.name: financial support is structured as part of the
benefits.detail: The financial support is structured as part of the resolution plan, where the successful resolution applicant infuses funds to settle claims of operational and financial creditors, pay CIRP costs, and provide performance guarantees (typically 10% of the resolution plan value).

benefits.name: quantum of financial support varies case-by-case based on
benefits.detail: The quantum of financial support varies case-by-case based on the resolution plan approved by the Committee of Creditors and the Adjudicating Authority.

documents.name: Declaration under Section 29A of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016
Proof of consent of financial creditors (not less than 66% by value)
Certificate of incorporation of the corporate debtor
Details of claims of financial and operational creditors
Performance guarantee (as per regulation 36B(4A) of CIRP Regulations)

application.implementing_agency: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India
application.deadline: The application for initiation of PPIRP must be filed before the Adjudicating Authority after the resolution plan is approved by the Committee of Creditors. There is no fixed window; the process can be initiated at any time subject to eligibility. However, once initiated, the resolution process must be completed within 90 days from the date of application, extendable by the Adjudicating Authority for a further 60 days in exceptional circumstances, making a maximum of 150 days.

schemes.schemeName: Tax Collected at Source (TCS) Exemption for Startups
schemes.officialName: Tax Collected at Source (TCS) Exemption for Startups
schemes.description: Tax Collected at Source (TCS) Exemption for Startups is a tax benefit under the Income Tax Act, 1961 that allows eligible startups to be exempt from TCS on certain specified transactions, reducing their compliance burden and improving cash flow during early growth stages.
schemes.objective: - Reduce tax compliance burden on startups - Improve working capital availability for early-stage enterprises - Encourage formalization and digital transactions among startups - Support ease of doing business for innovative ventures
schemes.ministry: Income Tax Department, Ministry of Finance, Government of India

all.detail: Startups recognized by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) under the Startup India initiative are eligible for TCS exemption on specified goods and services as per the provisions of the Income Tax Act, 1961.

benefits.name: Exemption from Tax Collected at Source
benefits.detail: Exemption from Tax Collected at Source (TCS) on specified transactions such as sale of overseas tour packages, foreign remittances, and sale of alcohol, thereby reducing upfront tax outflow and improving liquidity for eligible startups.

benefits.name: scheme provides indirect financial support by exempting eligible
benefits.detail: The scheme provides indirect financial support by exempting eligible startups from paying TCS on certain specified transactions, thereby retaining more working capital that would otherwise be blocked as tax deducted at source.

documents.name: Details of specified transactions attracting TCS

application.implementing_agency: Income Tax Department, Ministry of Finance, Government of India
application.deadline: Rolling basis — applications can be submitted throughout the financial year as and when TCS-liable transactions occur.

schemes.description: The Startup GST Exemption & Composition Scheme is a tax benefit initiative under the Goods and Services Tax (GST) framework designed to reduce compliance burden and tax liability for eligible startups.
schemes.objective: - Reduce tax compliance burden for startups - Lower GST liability through composition scheme rates - Simplify return filing and record-keeping requirements - Encourage formalization of startup businesses under GST - Support cash flow management for early-stage enterprises
schemes.ministry: Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN) under the guidance of the GST Council and Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)

all.detail: Startups with an aggregate annual turnover not exceeding INR 1.5 Crore in the preceding financial year are eligible to opt for the GST Composition Scheme.

benefits.name: Eligible startups benefit from reduced GST rates
benefits.detail: Eligible startups benefit from reduced GST rates (1% for manufacturers and traders, 5% for restaurants), quarterly return filing (GSTR-4) instead of monthly, simplified compliance with minimal record-keeping, and lower tax outflow compared to regular GST rates.

benefits.name: scheme also eliminates the need to issue tax
benefits.detail: The scheme also eliminates the need to issue tax invoices and maintain detailed input tax credit records.

benefits.name: Under the Composition Scheme, startups pay GST at a
benefits.detail: Under the Composition Scheme, startups pay GST at a concessional rate of 1% (for manufacturers and traders) or 5% (for restaurants) on their turnover, instead of the standard GST rates.

benefits.name: This results in direct tax savings, improving cash flow
benefits.detail: This results in direct tax savings, improving cash flow.

benefits.name: There is no direct financial grant or subsidy
benefits.detail: There is no direct financial grant or subsidy

benefits.name: benefit is in the form of reduced tax
benefits.detail: the benefit is in the form of reduced tax liability.

documents.name: Declaration of eligibility for Composition Scheme
Bank account details linked to GSTIN

application.implementing_agency: Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN) under the guidance of the GST Council and Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)
application.deadline: The option to opt for the Composition Scheme must be exercised before the commencement of the financial year for which it is sought, or within 30 days of obtaining GST registration. Once opted, it remains valid unless withdrawn or disqualified.

schemes.schemeName: ESOP Tax Deferment for Startup Employees
schemes.officialName: ESOP Tax Deferment for Startup Employees
schemes.description: The ESOP Tax Deferment for Startup Employees scheme allows eligible startups to defer tax on Employee Stock Option Plans (ESOPs) and sweat equity shares, enabling employees to pay tax only upon sale of shares or exit from the company, thereby reducing early financial burden and promoting…
schemes.objective: - Defer tax on ESOPs and sweat equity shares for startup employees - Reduce early-stage financial burden on employees receiving equity compensation - Promote employee retention and long-term engagement in startups - Align tax treatment with actual realization of gains from equity holdings - Support wealth creation for employees in high-growth startups
schemes.ministry: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

all.detail: The employer must be a DPIIT-recognised startup under Section 140 of the Income Tax Act, 2025, incorporated on or after 1st April 2016 and before 1st April 2030, with turnover not exceeding ₹300 crore in the relevant tax year, and engaged in innovation, development, or improvement of products, processes, or services, or having a scalable business model with high potential for employment generation or wealth creation.

benefits.name: Tax deferment on ESOPs and sweat equity shares until
benefits.detail: Tax deferment on ESOPs and sweat equity shares until the earlier of: expiry of 60 months from the end of the relevant tax year, sale of shares by the employee, or exit from the company.

benefits.name: Employees are not required to pay tax at the
benefits.detail: Employees are not required to pay tax at the time of exercising the option or receiving sweat equity shares, thereby improving cash flow and aligning tax liability with actual financial benefit realization.

benefits.name: scheme provides tax deferment, not direct financial support
benefits.detail: The scheme provides tax deferment, not direct financial support.

benefits.name: benefit lies in postponing tax liability on the
benefits.detail: The benefit lies in postponing tax liability on the perquisite value of ESOPs or sweat equity shares until a liquidity event (sale or exit), allowing employees to use the full value of their equity compensation without immediate tax outgo.

schemes.ministry: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

benefits.detail: Startups shall be allowed to self-certify compliance with 6 labour laws and 3 environmental laws through a simple online procedure.

benefits.name: In the case of environment laws, startups that fall
benefits.detail: In the case of environment laws, startups that fall under the ‘white category’ (as defined by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)) would be able to self-certify compliance, and only random checks would be carried out in such cases.

schemes.schemeName: Three-Year Tax Holiday for DPIIT Startups (80IAC)
schemes.officialName: Three-Year Tax Holiday for DPIIT Startups (80IAC)
schemes.description: The Three-Year Tax Holiday for DPIIT Startups (80IAC) provides eligible startups with a 100% income tax exemption for three consecutive financial years out of their first ten years of incorporation.
schemes.objective: - Provide tax relief to eligible startups during their initial years of operation - Encourage innovation and entrepreneurship by reducing financial burden - Support job creation and economic growth through startup ecosystem development - Promote long-term sustainability of startups by improving cash flow in early stages - Align tax policy with the Startup India initiative to foster a conducive environment for new ventures
schemes.ministry: Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, Government of India

all.detail: To be eligible for deduction under section 80-IAC, an entity must be a startup certified by the Inter-Ministerial Board (IMB), incorporated as a private limited company or a limited liability partnership (LLP) or a registered partnership firm, have been incorporated on or after 1st April, 2016 but before 1st April, 2025, and have an annual turnover not exceeding INR 100 crore in any of the financial years preceding the year in which deduction is claimed.

benefits.name: 100% deduction of profits and gains from eligible business
benefits.detail: 100% deduction of profits and gains from eligible business for three consecutive assessment years out of ten years beginning from the year of incorporation.

benefits.name: This results in complete income tax exemption for the
benefits.detail: This results in complete income tax exemption for the selected three years.

benefits.detail: The benefit is available only after obtaining certification from the Inter-Ministerial Board (IMB) established by DPIIT.

benefits.detail: The scheme provides a tax holiday in the form of 100% income tax exemption on profits from eligible business for three consecutive years.

benefits.detail: There is no direct cash disbursement

benefits.name: benefit is realized through reduced tax liability when
benefits.detail: the benefit is realized through reduced tax liability when filing income tax returns.

benefits.name: quantum of support depends on the startup's profits

schemes.description: The Presumptive Taxation Scheme under Section 44AD of the Income-tax Act, 1961 is designed for small businesses, including MSMEs, to simplify tax compliance by allowing them to declare income at a prescribed rate (8% of turnover or 6% for digital transactions) without maintaining detailed books…
schemes.objective: - Simplify tax compliance for small businesses by eliminating the need to maintain detailed books of accounts - Reduce the burden of tax audit under Section 44AB for eligible taxpayers - Promote ease of doing business through a presumptive income taxation model - Encourage digital transactions by offering a lower presumptive rate (6%) for income received via digital modes - Broaden the tax base by bringing small traders and service providers into the tax net with minimal compliance

schemes.description: The GST QRMP Scheme for MSMEs allows eligible small taxpayers to file GSTR-3B and GSTR-1 returns on a quarterly basis while paying taxes monthly.
schemes.objective: - Reduce compliance burden for small taxpayers - Allow quarterly filing of GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B returns - Enable monthly tax payment via PMT-06 for better cash flow management - Simplify GST return process for MSMEs with turnover up to INR 5 crores
schemes.ministry: Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN) under the oversight of the GST Council and the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)

all.detail: Taxpayers having an aggregate annual turnover of up to INR 5 crores in the preceding financial year are eligible to opt into the QRMP scheme.

benefits.detail: Quarterly filing of GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B returns reduces the frequency of return submission from monthly to quarterly.

benefits.detail: Taxpayers pay tax monthly using Form PMT-06, ensuring steady cash outflow compliance.

benefits.name: scheme reduces the administrative burden of frequent filings
benefits.detail: The scheme reduces the administrative burden of frequent filings while maintaining regular tax payment discipline.

benefits.name: It is particularly beneficial for small businesses seeking simpler
benefits.detail: It is particularly beneficial for small businesses seeking simpler compliance under GST.

benefits.name: QRMP scheme does not provide direct financial support
benefits.detail: The QRMP scheme does not provide direct financial support, subsidies, or grants.

benefits.name: Instead, it offers a procedural benefit by allowing eligible
benefits.detail: Instead, it offers a procedural benefit by allowing eligible taxpayers to file returns quarterly while continuing to pay tax on a monthly basis through Form PMT-06.

benefits.detail: There is no fund allocation, grant amount, or loan component associated with this scheme.

application.implementing_agency: Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN) under the oversight of the GST Council and the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)
application.deadline: Tax payment via PMT-06 is due monthly by the 25th of the following month. Quarterly returns (GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B) must be filed by the 22nd or 24th of the month following the quarter, depending on the taxpayer's category and state/UT. The option to opt into or opt out of the QRMP scheme must be exercised before the last day of the opening month of a quarter.

schemes.description: The Self Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers (SRMS) is a Central Sector Scheme launched in January 2007 by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, aimed at rehabilitating manual scavengers and their dependents by providing them with alternative…

all.detail: Beneficiaries must be Indian citizens and preferably belong to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, or Other Backward Classes, though the primary criterion is engagement in manual scavenging.

benefits.detail: Under SRMS, financial assistance is provided as a term loan up to a maximum of INR 15 lakhs per beneficiary for setting up self-employment units.

benefits.detail: The loan is extended at a concessional interest rate of 4% per annum.

schemes.objective: - To encourage/support academic collaborations - For development of products and technologies up to proof of concept - For validation of products/technologies towards commercialization - To stimulate technological innovation

all.detail: Eligibility Criteria for Industry/LLP as collaborator: Minimum 51% of the shares of the Company should be held by Indian Citizens holding Indian passport (Indian Citizens do not include Person of Indian Origin (PIO) and Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI) holders).
Minimum half of the persons who subscribed their names to the LLP document as its Partners should be Indian citizens.

benefits.name: Funding support
benefits.detail: Funding support (Grant): Total cost of the project must not exceed Rs. 50 lakhs (Non-recurring cost must not exceed 10% of the total cost).

benefits.name: IP rights may be with academia alone, or jointly
benefits.detail: IP rights may be with academia alone, or jointly shared between academia and industry (if academia establishes PoC with industry) as per the understanding between the two partners.

benefits.name: For CRS: Funding in the form of grant is
benefits.detail: For CRS: Funding in the form of grant is provided to both academic as well as industrial partners.

benefits.name: While funding is provided to the academia for In-House
benefits.detail: While funding is provided to the academia for In-House research which forms a part of validation of the Proof of Concept, funds are provided to the industrial partner for validation.

benefits.name: There is no ceiling to the funding
benefits.detail: There is no ceiling to the funding.

benefits.name: IPR: Although the IP rights reside with the academia
benefits.detail: IPR: Although the IP rights reside with the academia, the industry partner has first right of refusal for commercial exploitation of the New IP.

benefits.name: first right of refusal will be accompanied with
benefits.detail: The first right of refusal will be accompanied with an undertaking that its business strategy encompasses possibility of commercialization of the present technology under validation.

benefits.name: Funding Support
benefits.detail: Funding Support (Grant): Total cost of the project must not exceed Rs. 50 lakhs (Non-recurring cost must not exceed 10% of the total cost) for AIR.

benefits.detail: The pattern of assistance payable under the micro irrigation scheme will be 55% for small and marginal farmers and 45% for other farmers which will be met by both Central Government and State Government in the ratio of 60:40 for all states except the North Eastern and Himalayan states.

benefits.detail: In the case of these states, ratio of sharing is 90:10.

benefits.detail: The subsidy payable to the beneficiary will be limited to an overall ceiling of 5 hectare per beneficiary.

benefits.name: subsidy payment will be limited to the unit
benefits.detail: The subsidy payment will be limited to the unit costs specified in the scheme guidelines.

benefits.detail: 25% higher amounts have been taken into calculation of subsidy for the North Eastern and Himalayan states and 15% higher for states with low penetration of MI namely Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Union Territories.

schemes.description: Section 80IAC of the Income Tax Act provides a tax exemption to eligible startups for three consecutive assessment years out of their first ten years from incorporation.
schemes.objective: - Provide tax relief to startups during their initial years of operation - Encourage innovation and entrepreneurship in India - Support early-stage startups by reducing their tax liability - Promote sustainable business growth through fiscal incentives
schemes.ministry: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry

all.detail: The turnover of the startup must not exceed INR 100 crore in any of the financial years since incorporation.
The startup must obtain DPIIT recognition and subsequently secure approval from the Inter-Ministerial Board (IMB) set up by DPIIT.

benefits.name: 100% tax exemption on profits and gains derived from
benefits.detail: 100% tax exemption on profits and gains derived from eligible business for three consecutive assessment years out of the first ten years from incorporation.

benefits.name: exemption is available at the option of the
benefits.detail: The exemption is available at the option of the assessee for any three assessment years out of the ten years.

benefits.name: This benefit reduces the effective tax liability to zero
benefits.detail: This benefit reduces the effective tax liability to zero for the selected years, thereby improving cash flow and retained earnings for reinvestment.

benefits.name: scheme provides a direct financial benefit in the
benefits.detail: The scheme provides a direct financial benefit in the form of tax savings, where eligible startups can claim exemption from paying income tax on their profits for up to three years.

benefits.name: quantum of support is equivalent to the tax
benefits.detail: The quantum of support is equivalent to the tax amount that would have been payable on the profits from eligible business during the exempted years, calculated at the applicable corporate tax rate.

benefits.name: There is no upper monetary cap on the exemption
benefits.detail: There is no upper monetary cap on the exemption amount, as it is based on actual profits.

documents.name: Details of nature of business highlighting innovation, scalability, and employment/wealth creation potential
Declaration regarding turnover not exceeding INR 100 crore
Any other documents as may be required by the IMB

application.implementing_agency: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry
application.deadline: Applications for IMB approval can be made at any time; there is no fixed deadline. However, the tax exemption must be claimed in the income tax return for the relevant assessment year within the time allowed under the Income Tax Act.

schemes.description: Composite bank loans of Rs.10 lakh to Rs.1 crore for greenfield enterprises by at least one SC/ST borrower and at least one woman borrower per bank branch.
schemes.objective: To promote entrepreneurship among SC/ST and women; to facilitate greenfield enterprise creation in manufacturing, services, trading and agri-allied sectors; and to enable branch-level inclusion through mandated loan support.
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Finance, Government of India (Department of Financial Services), facilitated by SIDBI

exclusions.detail: existing-business expansion is not covered — scheme funds first-time (greenfield) ventures only
defaulters to any bank or financial institution are not eligible
applicants who are neither SC/ST nor women fall outside the scheme's target branches
loans below Rs.10 lakh or above Rs.1 crore are outside Stand-Up India's band (other schemes such as PMMY/PSB loans cover other bands)

benefits.name: Composite bank loan (term loan + working capital)
benefits.note: primary security/mortgage of project assets may be required by bank as per its lending norms
benefits.interest_rate: as per bank policy (not fixed by scheme)
benefits.duration: as per bank policy

contribution.margin_money_sources: central/state government schemes or beneficiary's own contribution (per scheme norms on Standup Mitra)

conditions: not a defaulter to any bank/financial institution

benefits.name: Handholding support
includes: connection to banks and support agencies

benefits.name: RuPay debit card for working capital withdrawal

documents.name: Caste certificate (SC/ST)
documents.condition: applicants claiming the SC/ST eligibility branch

documents.name: Project report / business plan
documents.condition: bank appraisal of the greenfield venture

documents.name: Declaration of not being a defaulter to any bank/financial institution
Trade licences / registrations as applicable to the activity
Skill/training certificate (where relevant to the activity)

application.ministry: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance (facilitation by SIDBI)
application.implementing_agency: all scheduled bank branches (RBL/RRB/Cooperative) with SIDBI as scheme facilitator
other_channels: Udyami helpline (facilitation, listed on Standup Mitra)
application.deadline: none (rolling)
